title: Left exactness of the canonical sheaf pullback in arbitrary coefficient universes
statement: For any scheme X, any functor i from its opens to its small etale category, continuity and representable flatness imply that the canonical pullback of sheaves of sets in Type (max (u + 1) v) preserves finite limits, for every universe v.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00X5, with filtered-colimit argument in arbitrary larger universes

proof.text: Install the given continuity hypothesis as an instance. Restrict the AB5 instance for Type (max (u + 1) v) to filtered indexing categories with objects and morphisms in universe u using CategoryTheory.AB5OfSize_of_univLE. Apply the already proved CategoryTheory.preservesFiniteLimits_op_lan_of_flat from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Flat to i: this is the universe-general version of the sectionwise filtered-colimit argument for presheaf pullback. Finally apply CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.preservesFiniteLimits. That theorem composes the limit-preserving sheaf inclusion, left Kan extension, and sheafification and transfers preservation across sheafPullbackIso, obtained from uniqueness of the left adjoint. Thus the original arbitrary-universe canonical sheaf pullback preserves finite limits.

theorem zariski_to_etale_sheaf_left_exact
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (i : X.Opens ⥤ X.Etale)
    (hcont : i.IsContinuous (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) X.smallEtaleTopology)
    [RepresentablyFlat i] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (i.sheafPullback (Type (max (u + 1) v))
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) X.smallEtaleTopology)
